🤔 𝐒𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐨

✔️ Find employees whose salary is greater than their manager’s salary. 
✔️ This is a classic self-join interview question.

📍 𝐈𝐧𝐩𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 : 𝐞𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐲𝐞𝐞𝐬

𝐞𝐦𝐩_𝐢𝐝|𝐞𝐦𝐩_𝐧𝐚𝐦𝐞|𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫_𝐢𝐝|𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐲
1|Raj|null|200000
2|Anita|1|150000
3|Vikram|1|220000
4|Neha|2|160000
5|Suresh|2|140000
6|Meena|3|230000

📊 𝐓𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 : 𝐬𝐪𝐥

👉 CREATE TABLE employees (
    emp_id     INT,
    emp_name   VARCHAR(50),
    manager_id INT,
    salary     NUMERIC(12,2)
);

👉 INSERT INTO employees VALUES
(1,'Raj',NULL,200000),
(2,'Anita',1,150000),
(3,'Vikram',1,220000),
(4,'Neha',2,160000),
(5,'Suresh',2,140000),
(6,'Meena',3,230000);

📤 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐩𝐮𝐭

𝐞𝐦𝐩_𝐢𝐝|𝐞𝐦𝐩_𝐧𝐚𝐦𝐞|𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐲|𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫_𝐧𝐚𝐦𝐞|𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫_𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐲
3|Vikram|220000|Raj|200000
4|Neha|160000|Anita|150000
6|Meena|230000|Vikram|220000

💡 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 / 𝐨𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

✔️ A self-join allows comparing each employee with their manager row directly.
✔️ In Spark, projecting only the needed manager columns before the join reduces shuffle and memory footprint.
